questions.q: What is the one strict rule that defines a staging model?
options: One staging model per source table, no joins, no aggregation
It must contain at least one JOIN to another staging model
It must aggregate data down to a single summary row
It must be materialized as a table, never a view
questions.explain: Staging models are 1:1 with a source table — no joins, no aggregation, only light cleanup.

questions.q: Which of these belongs in a staging model?
options: Renaming a column and casting its type
Joining orders to customers
Computing a customer's lifetime order count
Deciding what counts as an 'active' customer
questions.explain: Renaming columns and type casting are the light cleanup tasks staging models are for; joins, aggregation, and business logic belong to later layers.

questions.q: If a model joins two source tables together, what does this lesson say about calling it a staging model?
options: It's no longer a staging model — it's an intermediate model
It's still a valid staging model as long as the join is small
Staging models are required to contain at least one join
The distinction doesn't matter in practice
questions.explain: A join disqualifies a model from being 'staging' — that logic belongs to the intermediate layer covered in Chapter 3.

questions.q: Why does keeping column renames confined to the staging layer matter?
options: A rename only needs to happen in one place, and every downstream model can assume clean, consistent columns
It makes the SQL run faster in the warehouse
Renaming columns is not actually allowed anywhere else in dbt
It has no practical benefit beyond convention
questions.explain: Because every downstream model refs the staging model rather than the raw source, a rename only needs to happen once, and everything downstream can rely on it.

questions.q: What is the standard naming pattern for a staging model, per this lesson?
options: stg_<source_name>__<table_name>, e.g. stg_jaffle_shop__orders
model_<table_name>_final
raw_<table_name>_v2
<table_name>_staging_temp
questions.explain: The convention used across real dbt projects is stg_<source>__<table>, with two underscores separating the source and table names.
